## Document ID

Document ID CU1587

## Version

Version 5.0

## Status

Status Published

## Published Date

Published Date 09/01/2024

Title

What is the difference between each type of membership?

Body

Executive Membership:

- $130.00 Annual membership fee ($65 membership fee, plus $65 upgrade fee)*
- Includes a free Household Card
- Valid at all Costco locations worldwide
- Annual 2% Reward on qualified Costco purchases (terms and conditions apply)
- Additional benefits and greater savings on Costco Services
- Extra benefits on select Costco Travel products

Business Membership:

- $65.00 Annual membership fee*
- Includes a free Household Card
- Add Affiliate Cardholders for $65 each*
- Valid at all Costco locations worldwide
- Purchase for resale
- Business Members must provide Costco with the appropriate resale information

Gold Star Membership:

- $65.00 Annual membership fee*
- Includes a free Household Card
- Valid at all Costco locations worldwide

You can find more details on each type of membership and even sign up right here. Please keep in mind that the Costco double guarantee applies to all membership levels. That means we guarantee both your membership and our products with a refund†, if they don’t meet your satisfaction.

*Plus applicable sales tax.

†Limitations apply. See the membership counter or Costco.com for details.

# Membership Fee Increase

## Document ID

Document ID CU2664

## Version

Version 5.0

## Status

Status Published

## Published Date

Published Date 09/01/2024

Title

Membership Fee Increase

Body

Effective September 1, 2024, membership fees have increased.

| | Old Fee | New Fee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gold Star | $60 | $65 |
| Business | $60 | $65 |
| Business Add-on/Affiliate | $60 | $65 |
| *Executive | $120 | $130 |

All Costco memberships will continue to include one free card for a designated member of the household who is 16 years of age or over.

Our membership fees help to offset operational costs so we can keep our prices low. A modest increase in fees will allow us to bring our members even greater value. To learn more about why we charge a membership fee, click here.

New Sign-upsNew members will be charged the new fee structure effective Sept.1, 2024.

Renewals The fee increase took place beginning with September 2024 renewals, which members began receiving in mid-July.

Auto Renew Memberships that are auto renewed will be charged the new fee effective Sept. 1, 2024.

UpgradesAll Executive upgrades will be based on the new fee structure effective Sept. 1, 2024.

Executive Effective Sept. 1, we also increased the cap on the Executive Membership 2% Reward from $1,000 per year to $1,250 per year.

# What is an Executive Membership?

## Document ID

Document ID CU1483

## Version

Version 11.0

## Status

Status Published

## Published Date

Published Date 03/16/2026

Title

What is an Executive Membership?

Body

It pays to be a Costco Executive Member:

Executive Members earn an annual 2% Reward on qualifying purchases at Costco, Costco.com, and Costco Travel. Plus, additional benefits are available on our suite of Costco Services. We offer a 100% satisfaction guarantee and will cancel and refund membership fees at any time if a member is dissatisfied.

Additional values are available to Executive Members such as earlier shopping hours, lower prices on check printing, auto buying, roadside assistance included at no charge for vehicles covered through the Auto Insurance program and additional travel benefits. View our full list of Costco Services. Additionally, Executive Members can save using Instacart.

Costco membership is $65 a year. An Executive Membership is an additional $65 upgrade fee per year. Each includes a free Household Card. Please include sales tax in all applicable states. (Business Members also pay an additional $65 for each additional cardholder - purchases made by the additional cardholders do not contribute towards the 2% Reward.) Members who upgrade for a partial year will be charged a prorated upgrade fee.

The Primary Member or Account Manager of an existing membership may upgrade to the Executive membership one of the following ways:

- Online – Sign In or Register on Costco.com, then visit Account Details. Once your membership has been verified, you may upgrade your membership.
- In Person – Visit any Costco membership counter.
- By Phone – Call Member Services at 1-800-774-2678.

When to expect a 2% Reward Certificate:

The 2% Reward Certificate is mailed with the renewal notice approximately two months prior to the member’s annual renewal date. A member must be a paid Executive Member at the time the Reward is issued to receive the certificate. Members who reverse their Executive status will lose all rewards accumulated. Rewards are not prorated.

Eligible purchases:

Only purchases made by the Primary and active Primary Household Cardholder on the account will apply toward the Reward. Most U.S. warehouse purchases apply to the 2% Reward. Please see below for a list of ineligible purchases. Eligible purchases made in Canada, Puerto Rico or on Costco.com also contribute to the annual 2% Reward. For eligible Costco Travel purchases, Executive Members will earn a 2% Reward after travel is completed (must be an Executive Member when travel starts).

In most cases, pharmacy and over the counter (OTC) purchases apply to the 2% Reward. Only the amount not covered by insurance (co-pay) is calculated as part of the 2% Reward.

Refunds of eligible purchases will be deducted from the 2% Reward.

Ineligible purchases:

Purchases made in Australia, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Spain, Taiwan, Iceland, China, France and the U.K. will not be applied to the 2% Reward.

The following purchases do not apply to the 2% Reward:

- Alcohol in AL, AZ, AR, CA, CT, GA, HI, KS, KY, MA, MI, MN, MS, NH, NC, ND, OH, OK, RI, SD, TN, TX, UT, and VT
- Auto Purchasing
- Battery Fees
- Bottle Deposit
- Cell Phones, Cell Phone Accessories and Cell Phone Service Contracts (purchased through 3rd parties)
- Costco Shop Cards/Gift of Membership
- Children’s Miracle Network Hospital Balloons and other charitable giving Costco.com
- Shipping Fees
- Costco Services
- Food Court
- Gasoline
- Home Delivery Services (Delivery Charges, Installation)
- Membership Fees
- Misc. Taxes & Fees
- Oil Disposal Fees
- Optical Exams
- Stamps
- Tire Balance & Installation Fees
- Tire Disposal Fees
- Tobacco
- Websites not hosted by Costco.com including online Costco Photo Center
- 3rd Party Insurance Payments
- Prescription drug purchases in certain states (including Arkansas, New Jersey, and New York)

results.title: Costco Membership Cost and Benefits: Is It Worth It?
results.author: Amanda Barroso Lead Writer & Content Strategist
results.text:
Costco Membership Cost and Benefits: Is It Worth It? - NerdWallet

Is a Costco membership really worth the annual fee?

Lots of people seem to think so. Costco boasted more than 145 million members in 2025 and has a U.S. renewal rate of over 90%.

[1]

Costco. Costco Wholesale 2025 Annual Report. Accessed Jul 22, 2026.

View all sources

While bulk groceries get the most attention, Costco’s savings can extend far beyond what ends up in your cart, from car repairs and contact lenses to travel packages and home appliances.

Here's a breakdown of what a Costco membership gets you, so you can decide if adding one more annual fee to your budget is worth it.

## Costco membership price

Costco charges annual membership fees, which start at $65. In return, members get access to discounted prices on items.

Here’s a quick glance at what each membership tier offers:

| | Gold Star ($65/yr) | Business ($65/yr) | Executive ($130/yr) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who it's for | Personal use | Business owners | Personal or business |
| Cards included | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Valid at all locations and Costco.com | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Can add extra cardholders | No | +$65/each | +$65/each |
| Early store access | No | No | 1 hr. early (Sun-Fri), 30 min. early (Sat) |
| Annual 2% reward | No | No | Up to $1,250 on qualified purchases |

## Is Costco worth it?

Let’s do some rough math to figure it out.

Costco charges a baseline price of $65 just to walk through the door. Spread out that membership cost across a full year, and you’ll need to save $5.42 per month for it to be financially “worth it.”

That’s a pretty low bar.

If you can save even $0.10 per gallon of gas, that’s $1.50 on 15 gallons. If you fill up every week, that’s $6 in savings right there.

A family of four spends between $1,000-$1,600 every month in groceries, according to USDA data. Costco wouldn’t account for all of that spending, but even if a family spends $500 a month ($6,000 a year), you’d only need to save 1% on purchases to break even. Costco advertises a 15%-20% savings compared with national brands.

### Meet MoneyNerd, your weekly news decoder

So much news. So little time. NerdWallet's new weekly newsletter makes sense of the headlines that affect your wallet.

SUBSCRIBE FOR FREE

Here are other ways to decide if a membership might be a good value:

### ✅ A Costco membership might be worth it if you:

Have kids, roommates or a larger family to shop for

Live near a Costco

Own a car and can use the Costco gas station regularly

Have storage space for bulk goods and freezer items

Book travel or rent cars occasionally

Plan to buy an appliance in the next year or two

Need affordable access to health care experts and care

- Costco membership perks beyond the warehouse

### ❌ A Costco membership might not be worth it if you:

Live alone

Have limited freezer and/or storage space

Don’t have easy access to a Costco location

Shop impulsively

Already have a membership to another warehouse store like Sam’s Club or BJ’s

» MORE: How to save on groceries

I have a Gold membership, and there are things I love — the premade food is easy to grab for busy nights, and I feel like I’m getting good quality items for my money. I also trust the Kirkland store brand and appreciate Costco's workplace policies.

Costco's return policy is unmatched. I recently returned an air mattress that was a couple of years old because it got a hole — no questions asked. And getting to try the samples while I shop is always a plus.

But, I feel like the store opens too late (with young children, I’ve already lived three lives by 10 a.m.), and the line to checkout is always long. If Costco added Scan and Go like Sam’s Club, I’d never shop at another warehouse.

## Costco membership perks beyond the warehouse

The food court: Costco is known for its $1.50 hot dog and soda combo, but its newest menu item — chicken tenders with dipping sauce for $6.99 — is making headlines and getting mentions on social media. The store's other popular items include a slice of pepperoni or cheese pizza ($1.99), a chicken bake ($3.99) and the double chocolate chunk cookie ($2.49). Get your kids a slice of pizza before you shop to keep them busy, like I do.

Travel deals: Members can visit Costco’s travel website to book vacation packages, hotels, cruises and rental cars. There are even theme park deals for all the Disney lovers out there.

Pharmacy: Members can get discounts on their prescriptions, schedule immunizations and pick up pet medications at lower prices. You might be trading some convenience (no drive-thru window here), but there’s a mail order option.

Shutterfly: Members save 51% on every Shutterfly order and get free economy shipping if they spend more than $30. The discount is added right to your cart (no coupon code needed). Just be sure to add your membership to your Shutterfly account to take advantage of the deal.

Sesame: Members can schedule virtual urgent care visits for $34, pay $65 for virtual therapy and more — including subscriptions for mental health, women’s health, weight loss and prescription skincare.

Home appliances: There are some benefits to buying appliances from Costco. Delivery and installation are included in the price, and Costco will haul away your old model. There’s a two-year warranty included and you can earn up to 4% in rewards.

Costco Auto Program: You might already know you can get car repairs done at Costco, and even new tires. But Costco sells cars, too. They have new and used vehicles and better deals for Executive members. Plug in your ZIP code to get a list of participating Costco dealers and local incentives.

If you’re thinking about how to leverage your Costco trip for points or credit card rewards, you might be able to earn more money back with the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi. Compare that credit card with other cash-back cards you may already carry.

Nerdy Perspective

I’ve been a Costco member since the year 2000. Over the years Costco has helped me save on car rentals; eyeglasses and contacts; tires; Pokémon cards; 800-thread-count sheets; diapers for my babies; two Dyson vacuums; countless photo calendars and Christmas cards; sleds; houseplants; appliances and electronics; giant slabs of wild king salmon; big ol’ jugs of Canadian maple syrup; and hunks of Gruyere. I use the home delivery service more often than I shop in-person, because, as any longtime fan knows, you don’t decide what you’re going home with from Costco: Costco decides for you!

Karen Gaudette Brewer

Head of Content, Core Personal Finance

Frequently Asked Questions

How to pay at Costco?How to pay at Costco?

Visa credit cards are the only credit card type accepted at brick-and-mortar Costco stores in the U.S. Costco also accepts debit/ATM cards, cash, checks and traveler's checks, EBT cards and mobile payment methods such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Costco.com accepts Mastercard in addition to Visa credit cards.

Costco allows members to bring up to two guests to shop at a warehouse, but only members can make purchases.

How do you sign up for a Costco membership?How do you sign up for a Costco membership?

To sign up, visit the membership desk at any location. You can also sign up online or by calling 1-800-774-2678.

Costco has an option to cancel your membership and receive a refund if you're dissatisfied.

Can I get a freebie membership?Can I get a freebie membership?

No. The samples are free, but Costco doesn’t provide free memberships. There are new-member promotions, such as digital shop cards, during promotional periods.

Certain groups might also qualify for discounts. Teachers, college students, medical professionals, military personnel, government employees and first responders may be eligible to receive a digital Costco gift card when they sign up.

Costco Wholesale Corporation - Costco Wholesale Corporation Reports June Sales Results and Announces Quarterly Cash Dividend and Plans for Membership Fee Increase

## Costco Wholesale Corporation Reports June Sales Results and Announces Quarterly Cash Dividend and Plans for Membership Fee Increase

07/10/2024

Download(opens in new window)PDF

ISSAQUAH, Wash., July 10, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Costco Wholesale Corporation (“Costco” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: COST) today reported net sales of $24.48 billion for the retail month of June, the five weeks ended July 7, 2024, an increase of 7.4 percent from $22.78 billion last year.

Net sales for the first 44 weeks were $210.55 billion, an increase of 6.9 percent from $196.93 billion last year.

Comparable sales were as follows:

| | 5 Weeks | 44 Weeks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U.S. | 5.6% | 4.4% |
| Canada | 5.2% | 7.3% |
| Other International | 4.3% | 8.5% |
| Total Company | 5.3% | 5.4% |
| E-commerce | 18.4% | 15.2% |

Comparable sales excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange were as follows:

| | 5 Weeks | 44 Weeks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U.S. | 6.3% | 4.8% |
| Canada | 8.4% | 8.1% |
| Other International | 8.7% | 8.1% |
| Total Company | 6.9% | 5.6% |
| E-commerce | 19.1% | 15.2% |

Additional discussion of these results is available in a pre-recorded message. It can be accessed by visiting investor.costco.com(click on “Events & Presentations”). This message will be available through 4:00 p.m. (PT) on Wednesday, July 17, 2024.

The Company also announced today that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend on Costco common stock of $1.16 per share. The quarterly dividend is payable August 9, 2024, to shareholders of record at the close of business on July 26, 2024.

The Company also announced that, effective September 1, 2024, it will increase annual membership fees by $5 for U.S. and Canada Gold Star (individual), Business, and Business add-on members. With this increase, all U.S. and Canada Gold Star, Business and Business add-on members will pay an annual fee of $65. Also effective September 1, annual fees for Executive Memberships in the U.S. and Canada will increase from $120 to $130 (Primary membership of $65, plus the Executive upgrade of $65), and the maximum annual 2% Reward associated with the Executive Membership will increase from $1,000 to $1,250. The fee increases will impact around 52 million memberships, a little over half of which are Executive. Costco currently operates 882 warehouses, including 609 in the United States and Puerto Rico, 108 in Canada, 40 in Mexico, 33 in Japan, 29 in the United Kingdom, 18 in Korea, 15 in Australia, 14 in Taiwan, seven in China, four in Spain, two in France, and one each in Iceland, New Zealand and Sweden. Costco also operates e-commerce sites in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, Japan and Australia.

(AP Photo/Gene J. Puskar, File)

# Costco Cash Back Rewards: What You Need To Know

[![Clever Dude](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/logos/light/aol_clever_dude_695.png)](https://www.cleverdude.com/)

Brandon Marcus

Thu, July 23, 2026 at 6:39 PM UTC

0

![Costco Cash Back Rewards: What You Need To Know](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/07/23/d136a489-787e-3a04-b714-b15082ac45d9/533fbb8f-5020-4cfc-aef7-2017fa8a36e8.webp)

Millions of Americans flock to Costco every year, looking for big deals and bigger rewards. Is a Costco membership really worth it in 2026? – Shutterstock

Two important things happen to many Costco members in February. First, it is often the month when the Costco membership renewal notification arrives, which may also include the Executive Membership 2% Reward certificate. Second, it is the month when cardholders receive the annual cash-back rewards from the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi. While both may be described as cash-back rewards, they are two separate rebates from very different programs available to Costco members.

That distinction matters because the rewards do not work exactly the same way, the earning limits have changed, and the amount a member needs to spend to justify an Executive upgrade is different from what it was a few years ago. Let’s examine, compare, and contrast both programs, along with how Costco stacks up against Sam’s Club and BJ’s Wholesale Club.

## Executive Membership Costco Cash Back Rewards

The standard [$65 Gold Star membership](https://www.costco.com/f/-/join-costco) gets shoppers through the Costco doors, while the Executive Membership [costs $130 per year and adds a 2% annual reward](https://www.costco.com/f/-/join-costco) on qualifying purchases at Costco warehouses, Costco.com, and qualifying Costco Travel purchases. The Executive Membership upgrade costs an additional $65 per year. The 2% reward can reach a maximum of $1,250 during a 12-month period.

The basic break-even calculation is straightforward. A member needs about $3,250 in qualifying annual purchases to generate $65 in rewards and recover the Executive upgrade fee. That is higher than the old $3,000 figure because Costco increased the membership price. A household that spends $5,000 on qualifying purchases, for example, would generate approximately $100 in Executive rewards, leaving about $35 in rewards after covering the $65 upgrade cost.

Costco sends the reward certificate with the renewal statement before the membership renewal date. The exact timing depends on the member’s renewal cycle, but Costco says the reward generally arrives roughly two and a half to three months before renewal. The certificate can be redeemed toward most merchandise purchases at Costco warehouse front-end registers, although Costco excludes certain purchases and the reward cannot simply be used like a general-purpose bank check.

The rules also matter if a member downgrades or cancels. Costco says an Executive Membership reward must be redeemed while the membership remains active, and canceling or downgrading can affect the treatment of the reward and any refund of the upgrade fee. The reward itself does not carry a standard expiration date, unlike the Costco credit card reward certificate.

One useful detail often gets overlooked: the Executive Membership reward and the Costco Anywhere Visa reward are separate. The Executive reward comes from the membership tier. The credit card reward comes from spending on the card. That means a qualifying $1,000 Costco purchase charged to the Costco Anywhere Visa can potentially earn 2% from the Executive Membership and another 2% from the card, for a combined 4% reward rate on that purchase.

## Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi

Costco members who have a [Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi](https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/costco-anywhere-visa-card) can earn cash-back rewards throughout the year by using the card for eligible purchases. The 2026 earning structure looks like this:

5% on gas purchased at Costco

4% on other eligible gas and EV charging purchases

5% and 4% rewards combined on the first $7,000 in annual eligible gas and EV charging spending, then 1% thereafter

3% on restaurants and eligible travel, including Costco Travel

2% on all other purchases at Costco and Costco.com

1% on all other purchases

The card has [no separate annual fee](https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/costco-anywhere-visa-card) as long as the cardholder maintains a paid Costco membership. The card also has no foreign transaction fees, according to Costco’s current benefit information.

The rewards arrive as an annual credit card reward certificate after the February billing statement closes. Unlike the Executive Membership reward, the Costco Anywhere Visa reward certificate generally must be redeemed by December 31 of the year it is issued. It can be used for merchandise at U.S. Costco warehouses or exchanged for cash at Costco, subject to the program’s rules.

That timing creates an easy mistake. Someone can receive two rewards around the same time and assume they represent one large Costco rebate. They do not. The Executive reward comes from eligible Costco spending during the membership year, while the Citi reward reflects eligible credit card spending during the card’s annual rewards period.

## Costco vs. Sam’s Club vs. BJ’s Wholesale Club

Costco is not the only warehouse club with a membership reward program. The best choice depends heavily on where a household shops, how much it spends, and whether it wants a co-branded credit card.

| Program | Membership Cost | Membership Reward | Store Credit Card Reward | Key Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Costco Executive | $130/year | 2% on qualifying purchases, up to $1,250 | Costco Anywhere Visa: 2% at Costco, 3% restaurants/travel, 5% Costco gas | Executive upgrade breaks even at about $3,250 in qualifying annual spending |
| Sam’s Club Plus | $120/year | 2% Sam’s Cash on qualifying purchases, up to $750 annually | Sam’s Club Mastercard: up to 5% gas, 3% dining, 3% Sam’s Club purchases for Plus members | Membership reward and card rewards are separate |
| BJ’s Club+ | $120/year | 2% back on most eligible BJ’s purchases, up to $500 per membership year | BJ’s One+ Mastercard: 5% at BJ’s and 2% elsewhere | Rewards do not expire while membership remains active |

[Sam’s Club Plus](https://www.samsclub.com/join) members earn 2% Sam’s Cash on qualifying in-club purchases, with a current annual limit of $750 according to Sam’s Club’s terms. The Sam’s Club Mastercard can add 5% back on gas for the first $6,000 annually, 3% on Sam’s Club purchases for Plus members, 3% on dining, and 1% on other purchases.

[BJ’s Club+ membership](https://www.bjs.com/membership/?srsltid=AfmBOopmcgn1UzQZ7AA6_30FKWl1oRg0gVRZ8GPW8WlsutwmU-xqqoI6) costs $120 per year and offers 2% back in rewards on most eligible BJ’s purchases, up to $500 per membership year. The BJ’s One+ Mastercard can add 5% back on most BJ’s purchases and 2% back on other purchases, while also offering a 15-cent-per-gallon fuel discount at BJ’s Gas.

The lesson is simple: the biggest advertised percentage does not automatically equal the best deal. A household that shops at Costco every week may get more value from Costco’s combination of the Executive reward and credit card. A household that spends heavily on gas may prefer a different structure. The math should follow actual shopping habits, not the biggest number in the advertisement.

## Maximize Your Rewards

Use this list before deciding whether to upgrade, apply for a card, or change where you shop:

Calculate annual qualifying warehouse spending. Add up realistic purchases, not spending created just to earn rewards.

Check the break-even point. Costco Executive members need about $3,250 in qualifying annual spending to generate $65 in rewards.

Separate membership rewards from credit card rewards. They are different programs with different rules.

Use the best card for each category. The Costco Visa offers different rates for gas, restaurants, travel, Costco purchases, and other spending.

Track annual caps. The highest reward rate usually applies only up to a spending limit.

Pay the credit card balance in full whenever possible. Interest charges can erase rewards very quickly.

Keep credit utilization under control. A good rewards strategy should not require carrying a balance or regularly pushing a credit card close to its limit.

Check the reward expiration date. The Costco credit card certificate and Executive Membership reward follow different rules.

Plan for large purchases. A qualifying laptop, appliance, mattress, or other major purchase can create a meaningful reward opportunity when the item already fits the budget.

The most important box on the list may be the one about credit utilization. Rewards are only useful when the interest cost does not swallow them. Someone who earns 2% or 3% in rewards but carries a balance at a high interest rate can lose far more money than the rewards provide. Keeping balances manageable, paying on time, and avoiding unnecessary applications for multiple cards generally makes more sense than chasing every available percentage point.

## Use Rewards For Big Purchases

Costco rewards can become especially useful when a planned purchase already appears on the household shopping list. Computers and laptops offer a good example. A shopper who needs a $1,500 [laptop](https://www.cleverdude.com/content/save-money-and-your-back-with-the-best-backpacks-for-work/) might earn 2% from a qualifying Executive Membership purchase and another 2% from the Costco Anywhere Visa, potentially producing $60 in combined rewards before considering any sale price or other promotion.

The same idea can apply to major [appliances](https://www.cleverdude.com/content/millions-still-do-this-with-household-appliances-experts-say-it-could-be-dangerous/), furniture, mattresses, televisions, and other large purchases sold through Costco. The key word is planned. Buying a $2,000 television solely to generate $80 in rewards does not create a bargain. Buying a television that was already needed and comparing Costco’s total price, warranty, return policy, and rewards can make the calculation much more useful.

Big purchases can also help a member reach the Executive Membership break-even point. Someone who normally spends $2,800 on qualifying purchases might cross the $3,250 threshold after buying a needed laptop or appliance. That purchase does not make the upgrade automatically worthwhile, but it can change the annual math.

The same principle applies to the other warehouse clubs. A Sam’s Club Plus member may benefit from a large qualifying in-club purchase that earns Sam’s Cash, while a BJ’s Club+ member may use a planned major purchase to generate additional rewards. The winning strategy involves comparing the final price and the reward structure together rather than focusing on the reward percentage alone.

## Get The Most Cash Back From Your Costco Membership

Recoup Your Executive Membership Fee: To recoup the $65 fee to upgrade to the executive membership, you’ll have to spend thousands annually at Costco. If your rewards check doesn’t exceed $65, you can go to customer service and receive the difference. This makes upgrading to the executive membership a can’t lose proposition.

Use Your Costco Anywhere Visa®: You earn cashback using your Costco Anywhere Visa®. Use it for every purchase possible, earn cash back, and pay the bill as soon as you get home.

Double Up Rewards By Shopping At Costco: Purchase as much of your necessities as possible at Costco using the Costco Anywhere Visa®. You’ll earn the 2% Executive Membership rewards AND the 2% cashback from the credit card cashback program. That’s a total of 4% cashback for everyday items you buy anyway!

Know What Costco Sells: Consider Costco when you’re looking for computers, small appliances, water heaters, indoor and outdoor furniture, mattresses, and even carpeting!

Don’t Forget Costco.com: Costco warehouses are huge, but they don’t contain everything Costco sells. You may be surprised at what else you can find at Costco.com that can help boost your rewards checks.

Joining the Costco club may make you feel special, like you’re part of an exclusive group. This is due to the [ingroup bias](https://practicalpie.com/ingroup-bias-definition-examples/), which psychologists say is an evolutionary advantage to help our communities thrive. In fact, you can even find Costco memes being shared among groups who share the membership.

These two programs provide an opportunity to earn Costco cash back rewards simply by changing where I buy my day-to-day necessities. I’m looking forward to earning as much cashback as possible using my Costco membership next year! If you’re [ready to become a Costco member](https://www.costco.com/f/-/join-costco), you can take the next steps here.
